questions.question: Reaction rate is defined as:
options: The change in concentration or amount of reactants or products per unit time
The total amount of product formed by a reaction
The time a reaction takes to finish
The energy released per mole of reactant

questions.question: A flask loses 2,2 g of CO₂ (M = 44 g·mol⁻¹) in the first 50 s of a reaction. The average rate over this interval is:
A reaction is fastest:
options: At the start, when reactant concentrations are highest

questions.question: Two experiments use identical amounts of reactants, but one runs much faster. Their final amounts of product are:
options: The same — rate and extent are different questions

subtopics.title: Collision Theory and the Factors That Change Rate

questions.question: An effective collision is one in which the particles collide:
options: At any speed, as long as they touch
With correct orientation AND energy at least equal to the activation energy

questions.question: Activation energy is:
options: The energy released when products form
The average kinetic energy of the particles
The minimum energy needed for a reaction to occur

questions.question: Grinding a solid reactant into powder increases the rate because:
options: More particles are exposed at surfaces, so more collisions occur per second

questions.question: Raising the temperature increases the rate MAINLY because:
options: A much larger fraction of collisions has energy above the activation energy

questions.question: On a volume-time graph for gas produced, the reaction rate at any moment is given by:
options: The gradient of the curve at that moment

questions.question: In the disappearing cross experiment, a SHORTER time for the cross to vanish means:
options: A faster reaction — the measure works as one over time

questions.question: Equal masses of powdered and chipped CaCO₃ react with the same excess acid. Their volume-time curves:
options: Start with different steepness but flatten at the same final volume
Both start slowly and speed up

questions.question: A curve that flattens at a LOWER plateau than another indicates:
options: Less reactant was available, so less product could form

questions.question: On a molecular energy distribution curve, the particles able to react are those:
options: At the peak of the curve
To the left of the activation energy line
To the right of the activation energy line

questions.question: When the temperature rises, the energy distribution curve:
options: Shifts toward higher energies and flattens, with the same total area
Grows taller with the same shape
Moves its activation energy line to the left

questions.question: A catalyst increases reaction rate by:
options: Shifting the energy distribution curve to the right
Giving every particle more kinetic energy
Providing an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy

questions.question: On the potential energy diagram, a catalyst changes:
options: The height of the activation energy hump only — ΔH stays the same

subtopics.title: How Fast Is Not How Far

questions.question: Loose sugar in hot tea dissolves in seconds; a cube in cold tea takes minutes. Once both are dissolved, the sweetness of the cups is:
options: Identical — the rate differed, the extent did not

questions.question: Reactions sprint at the start and slow toward the end because:
options: Reactant particles become scarcer, so encounters become rarer
The activation energy climbs during the reaction
Temperature always falls as reactions run

questions.question: On the classic two-curve graph, a steeper curve reaching the SAME plateau means the experiments differed in:
options: Rate only — for example powder instead of chips, or warmer acid

subtopics.title: Bumper Cars That Only Count When They Hit Hard

questions.question: In the bumper car picture, a collision "counts" only when the cars:
options: Hit hard enough and at the right angle

questions.question: Adding more cars to the same floor represents:
options: Raising the concentration — more collisions per second

questions.question: A boulder of calcium carbonate reacts slowly with acid because:
options: Boulders have a higher activation energy
Most of its particles are hidden inside, out of reach of collisions
Its particles carry too little charge

questions.question: The catalyst "opens a side gate" means it:
options: Adds extra particles to the reaction
Lowers the energy barrier without being used up
Removes the products as they form

subtopics.title: Reading the Story off the Graph

questions.question: On a rate graph, the three story words are:
options: Steepness for speed, the bend for slowing, the plateau for the finish
Height for speed, width for time, colour for extent
Start for extent, middle for rate, end for temperature
Gradient for extent, plateau for rate, bend for energy

questions.question: Powdered and chunky chalk of the same mass, in the same acid, give plateaus that are:
options: At the same height — faster never means more

questions.question: Halving the mass of chalk while keeping the acid in excess will:
options: Halve the final volume of gas — a lower plateau

questions.question: In the disappearing cross experiment, treating a BIG time as a BIG rate is wrong because:
options: The experiment measures extent, not rate
A long time means a slow reaction — rate behaves as one over time
